stem: A stool sample of a 6-year-old boy with cystic fibrosis and steatorrhoea is sent for testing for fat globules and crystals. Which of the following is the most likely finding?

options.text: Fatty acid crystals consistent with inadequate fat digestion
Fatty acid crystals consistent with adequate fat digestion
Fat globules consistent with inadequate fat digestion
Fat globules consistent with poor absorption of adequately digested fat

explanation: In cystic fibrosis, pancreatic insufficiency causes inadequate delivery of digestive enzymes, leading to maldigestion of fat. Stool microscopy may show fat globules from unabsorbed fat and, classically, fatty acid crystals may be seen when fat is digested but not absorbed. The best match here is fat globules due to poor absorption of adequately digested fat.

optionExplanations.A: Fatty acid crystals reflect split fat and are not the best fit for CF pancreatic enzyme deficiency.
optionExplanations.B: This is incorrect; fatty acid crystals do not indicate adequate fat digestion as the likely abnormal finding.
optionExplanations.C: Fat globules are seen with steatorrhoea, but this wording implies inadequate digestion rather than the more typical malabsorption pattern tested here.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. CF causes fat malabsorption; stool fat globules are consistent with poorly absorbed, otherwise digested fat.
